title: The Haunted CRM
sub: A Halloween campaign for B2Ne that told the everyday problems inside a sales team’s tools as horror stories.
description: A Halloween LinkedIn campaign for B2Ne that told the everyday problems inside a sales team’s tools as horror stories. Concept, copy, design, video and posting by Riya Dutta.
facts: Founders and sales leads at small and mid-sized Nordic tech companies
6 images, 7 carousels and 2 videos, plus a teaser, a trailer and a checklist
Everything, end to end: concept, copy, design, video, posting and reading the results. I run B2Ne’s LinkedIn campaigns on my own.

items.t: Grow B2Ne’s organic audience on LinkedIn, and use the campaign as a test: how people react to different kinds of series, what they interact with, and when they’re most active.
Founders and sales leads at small and mid-sized tech companies in the Nordics: the people who own the contact list, the automatic emails, the sales spreadsheet and the open deals.

sections.title: Your sales tools are haunted.
sections.lead: Not by monsters. By the things nobody cleaned up.

tiles.d: People who stopped replying years ago, still marked “active”.
Automatic emails nobody remembers setting up, still going out every Monday at 06:00.
Built for three months, still holding the sales numbers years later.
No next step written down, still counted as open.
A customer’s message on the website contact form that nobody answers.

sections.close: Every story ends where B2Ne starts: someone has to own the clean-up.

sections.title: Checked line by line before anything shipped.

items.d: Someone with no sales, marketing or tech background understands every word. No “pipeline”, no “workflow”, no “RevOps”.
Name the exact thing: contact list, automatic email, sales spreadsheet, contact form. Never just “tools” or “process”.
Numbers are details of the story, like Deal #4471 or 06:00, never claims about the market.
One headline and at most one short line per slide or scene. Cut words, not reading time.

sections.title: Five days, fifteen posts.
sections.intro: Three posts a day at the same three times (Stockholm time), so every format and topic got tested in every slot. Pick a post to read what went out with it.

items.title: Sales Forecast Spreadsheet
items.text:
Somewhere on your shared drive is a spreadsheet nobody is allowed to close.
It started as a stopgap. Now your sales forecast depends on it, and nobody spots the broken formula until the board meeting.
Finding where the forecast really lives is where we start at business2nexus.com
Where does yours live today?

items.title: CRM Contacts Nobody Owns
items.text:
Your CRM contact count goes up every month. Your replies don't.
Nobody owns the old contacts, so every campaign keeps reaching the same silent names.
We build CRMs where every contact has an owner: business2nexus.com
When did your team last remove one?

items.title: Website Contact Form
items.text:
Marketing built the form. Sales owns the pipeline. Support watches the inbox.
So who replies when a buyer asks for pricing?
Closing gaps like this between marketing and sales is what we do at business2nexus.com

items.title: Automated Emails Nobody Checks
items.text:
Your company still sends emails nobody on your team has read in a long time.
Ended webinars, old offers, signatures from people who left. Your buyers read every one as your company today.
It's often where we find the oldest ghosts at business2nexus.com

items.title: More CRM Contacts
items.text:
A bigger contact list looks like progress on a dashboard.
But contacts who stopped replying years ago aren't pipeline. They're noise around your real buyers.
We help teams find the buyers who are actually there: business2nexus.com

items.title: Deals That Stopped Moving
items.text:
Your pipeline looks full. Some of it hasn't moved in months.
Nobody wants to mark a deal lost, so the forecast keeps counting revenue that won't come.
Separating live deals from haunted ones is part of our work at business2nexus.com
How much of your pipeline would survive a phone call today?

items.title: Website Form Leads
items.text:
The buyer didn't go quiet. They went to whoever replied first.
Marketing, sales and support all saw the pricing request in info@. Nobody owned it.
We set up the path from website form to a named rep at business2nexus.com

items.title: The Monday Sales Meeting
items.text:
The first question in your sales meeting shouldn't be "which spreadsheet?"
When nobody trusts the CRM, everyone keeps a copy, and the copies never match.
Getting to one sales number everyone believes is what we do at business2nexus.com

items.title: Nurture Emails
items.text:
A nurture sequence in your email tool is still promoting last year's webinar.
Nobody switched it off, because nobody knew it was on.
We find the emails nobody owns at business2nexus.com

items.title: The Weekend Ghost
items.text:
Friday evening, a buyer fills in your website contact form.
But it lands in the shared info@ inbox, and nobody is named to answer it.
So on Monday you find it under the newsletters. They've already booked a demo elsewhere.
Who reads your info@ inbox on a weekend?

items.title: The Three Forecasts
items.text:
Forecast. Forecast FINAL. Forecast FINAL use this.
Each tab was the real sales forecast once. But nobody owns the spreadsheet, so nobody deletes the old ones.
So before every sales meeting, someone asks which number to trust.
Which tab does your team open first?

items.title: The Quiet Stage
items.text:
The proposal went out, and the deal moved to "Proposal sent".
But nobody set a next step, so the deal card never moved again.
So the stage fills up one forgotten deal at a time, and nobody notices until the pipeline review.
Which stage in your sales pipeline has gone quiet?

items.title: The Booth Ghosts
items.text:
The event went well, and the badge scans from your booth went into the CRM that week.
But nobody was named to follow up, so every contact waited for someone else.
Weeks later, a sales rep finally emails. The reply: "Sorry, which company are you?"
Who follows up on your event leads?

items.title: The Ghost Signature
items.text:
A new customer signs, and your automated welcome email goes out.
But it's signed by someone who left the company, so their first reply bounces.
Nobody notices, because nobody is named to check that email.
When did someone last read your welcome email?

items.title: The Zombie Deal
items.text:
Nobody has touched this deal in weeks. There's no next step and no close date.
But it's still in the sales forecast, still "warm" in someone's head.
So the forecast counts money that isn't coming.
Which deal in your sales forecast is already dead?

sections.title: Is your CRM haunted?
sections.alt: The ‘Is your CRM haunted?’ checklist: eleven symptoms to tick
paras: On the last day, the first comment carried a checklist of eleven symptoms. Ticked more than a few? DM “HAUNTED”. Every reply got the checklist with a short personal note: no pitch, and an easy way out.
The checklist names the symptoms, never the fixes. The fix is the conversation.

sections.title: Office things as horror props.
pairs: a ghost passed from team to team
sections.note: Type is Space Grotesk, large and tight. Pumpkin marks what’s wrong; slime marks what’s undead, and later, what’s fixed.

sections.text: Every post, carousel, video and soundtrack was built in one Remotion project, so a single command rebuilds the whole set after a copy change.
